proposal.summary: R4 is CM550's engine position and speed measurement data. The TPU channel 10 primary input and the channel 1 backup input each keep a ring of 32-bit pulse periods (pulse_period_table / pulse_period_table_backup, e2m 100C). Each ring has a write pointer, a pointer to its last entry, a pointer to the oldest entry of the one-cylinder average window, a one-cam-revolution sum and the average. Beside the rings are the TPU channel 0 missing tooth (PMM) function and its error status byte pair, the cylinder identification pulse check on TPU channel 1, the main / backup phase comparison (e2m 12A1 / 12A2), the lost-sensor durations with their fault limits in cm550_calculateEngineSpeed, and the TPU channel 3 angle pulse that Calterm calls the DZG pulse. 61 of the 114 rows get names from their Calterm records and every user (6 reuse CM848 names of the same mnemonic). 53 are skipped: 30 sit in RAM that no dumped code reaches and that holds zero (names carried over from the removed J90280.05 analysis), 14 are elements of the programmable power fueling curve table PPCVTB, and 9 are halves of 4-byte values or unreferenced words. No row lies in the EEPROM image 0x803b0a-0x804f93, so no name takes _cal.

roles.role: mc68k_crankFuelAndTimingBufferStore is the TPU channel 0 missing-tooth interrupt for engine_position_signal_configuration 2, installed at 0x808edc by mc68k_initializeTpuChannel0MissingToothInputMode2; it ends in RTE. It copies TPU_CH15_PARAM6 into CKSYERTY (high byte) and CKSYERTT (low byte). Error type 0xc0 sets cam sync state and crank sync state to 0, any other value sets them to 2. It then calls mc68k_configureTpuChannelsForSpeedMeasurementMode and acknowledges CISR bit 0. It neither stores fuel or timing nor uses a buffer.

roles.role: mc68k_dutyCycleMonitorIsrHandler is the TPU channel 1 cam sensor (CI) pulse interrupt for cam sync type 1, installed at 0x808ee0 by mc68k_initializeTpuChannel1BackupSpeedInput. It reads CMSNTTCU from TPU_CH1_PARAM5's low byte and reloads the CI lost countdown 0x80d2c2 from 0x807f9d. It classifies the pulse as wide (CMSNCU01) or narrow (CMSNCU02) and checks the primary pulse number 0x80ccea against EGPSCU01 / EGPICU02, setting the cam / crank sync states to 1 or 2. It maintains CKTTCUER and CMSNCUER with their status word 0 bit 1 / word 2 bit 0x800 faults. It then calls mc68k_resetSpeedMeasurementMode0. No duty cycle is monitored.
roles.discriminator: The only channel 1 handler that reads the pulse width; 0x1b30a reads the backup period and 0x1b4b2 only resets.
roles.cm848_counterpart: counterpart: mpc555_handleCamSignalInterrupt @ 0x457d0 (the TPU-A channel 1 cam signal handler; a different design)

roles.role: mc68k_initializeTpuChannel1BackupSpeedInput is the cam sync type 1 set-up (cm550_canRpmModeConfigInit when 0x807f2e-style cam sync type = 1). It clears cam sync state and status, fills the backup period ring (0x80d07c, 0x80d084, 0x80cd0c, 0x80d074, average_pulse_period_backup), and installs the cam sensor pulse handler 0x1af32 at 0x808ee0. It programs channel 1 function 0xd with PARAM0 = 0x4f and PARAM1 = 0x100.
roles.discriminator: PARAM0 0x4f and the cam sensor pulse handler; type 0 (0x1b1ea) uses PARAM0 0xb and the period handler 0x1b30a; type 2 (0x1b39a) installs the reset handler 0x1b4b2.

roles.role: mc68k_dutyCycleMonitorBufferInit is the cam sync type 2 TPU channel 1 set-up. It fills the backup period ring (0x80d07c, 0x80d084, 0x80cd0c, 0x80d074, average_pulse_period_backup), programs channel 1 function 0xd with PARAM0 0xb, installs mc68k_tpuChannel1SpeedMeasurementResetInterruptHandler (0x1b4b2) at 0x808ee0, and clears CSCMSYCU 0x80d2cc and the long at 0x80d2d2. No duty cycle is monitored.
roles.discriminator: The type 2 variant, whose handler only resets the speed measurement.

roles.role: cm550_rpmTimingDeltaComparatorWithReturn is the EPS main / backup phase check on the primary period. It is called by all four TPU channel 10 handlers (jsr at 0x19c58 / 0x19f52 / 0x1a6b8 / 0x1a908) and runs only while 0x80aa16 (the primary period was not the sync pulse) is 0. If the backup lost counter is 0 it sets ESMNIPER = 1. Otherwise, when the main and backup pulse numbers match, it stores ESPHDF and counts ESPLPHCU / ESNGPHCU against ESPLPHTD / ESNGPHTD / ESMXPHCU, clearing ESBUIPER / ESMNIPER at the limit.
roles.discriminator: Its body is identical to cm550_checkEnginePositionSensorPhaseOnBackupPeriod except the gate: 0x80aa16 and the backup lost counter here, 0x80aa18 and the main lost counter there.

roles.role: cm550_checkEnginePositionSensorPhaseOnBackupPeriod is the backup-period version of 0x1a1e0. It is gated on 0x80aa18 (the backup period was not the sync pulse) and sets ESBUIPER = 1 when the main lost counter is 0. The ESPHDF and counter logic is the same. No caller in the dumped ROM.
roles.discriminator: Backup gate; the current name already fits.

roles.role: cm550_calculateEnginePositionPhaseLag computes both phase lags: engine_position_pulse_0_phase_lag (0x80db66) = (ESPSPGIN + average_engine_speed x ESPSPGSL / 16 + ESCWAJ) / 16 and engine_position_normal_phase_lag (0x80db64) = (ESPGIN + average_engine_speed x ESPGSL / 16 + ESCWAJ) / 16. All are unsigned word reads with a rounding add of 15 before the signed shift.
roles.discriminator: Two lines from one speed input; the current name fits.

roles.role: cm550_calculateEngineSpeed runs every 10 ms (task phases 0 and 2 of the 4-frame set). It counts down the main / backup / external lost counters and computes main and backup rpm as ESCUCF01/02 divided by the average periods. It counts the main / backup / external / crank sync lost durations above ESFXSNTD against their MAX limits and sets their fault bits. It calls speed_measurement_function_pointer, then selects the speed source and EMA-filters engine_rpm_primary. Finally it scales the lost counter reload values by engine speed bands.
roles.discriminator: The periodic engine speed task; the interrupt handlers fill the period sums it reads.
roles.cm848_counterpart: counterpart: cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal @ 0x44374 (the same role: lost counters, main/backup speeds, filter; different code)

verdict.overall:
R4 judged: the 74 proposals (61 batch rows and 13 extras), plus two rows the investigator left out. The task lists the pulse 0 line rows 0x80847a / 0x80847c in scope, but they got neither a proposal nor a skip, so I give them names (engine_position_pulse_0_phase_lag_intercept / _slope, checked in cm550_calculateEnginePositionPhaseLag 0x26e8e).

How I checked: I re-derived every role from the disassembly of all its users. These were the four TPU channel 10 set-ups and handlers, the channel 0 PMM handlers 0x19f82 / 0x1a6e8, the channel 1 set-ups and handlers 0x1ae22 / 0x1af32 / 0x1b1ea / 0x1b30a / 0x1b39a, the phase checks 0x1a1e0 / 0x1a298, cm550_calculateEngineSpeed, cm550_detectEngineSpeedSensorSyncPulse, the TPU channel 3 angle pulse functions, the crank functions and the phase lag function. Widths come from abs_refs.py. Register-based accesses were checked with a (d16,An) sweep, which does find the known a2 / a0 accesses. Every final name is unique in CM550, and no row is in the EEPROM image, so none takes _cal.

Changes:
- 0x80deda: the investigator missed a CM848 reuse. CM848 has the same record (block 1008 +4, same length and description: Average_EPS_Sample_Period), so the row takes CM848's drivetrain_ratio_engine_period_average.
- 0x807f5c: renamed to engine_position_sensor_out_of_phase_count_limit. It is a calibration limit, not a counter, and the repository names limits *_count_limit.
- Comment errors fixed: 0x80d296 (it is the main-period check 0x1a1e0, not the backup-period check, that sets the main flag when the backup sensor is lost) and 0x807f51 (the bit is in status word 2, 0x806004, not word 0).
- Ambiguous bit notation fixed: 0x807ee2 / 0x807ee4 / 0x80d05e / 0x807f9a / 0x80d2bf wrote 'bit 4' or 'bit 1' for masks 0x4 and 0x1, or 'bits 2-3 are set' for 'either bit (mask 0xc)'.
- 0x80d0be / 0x80d0bc: the code clears both adjustments only on the REENTRY -> STOPPED transition (0x17dee), not whenever the engine stops.
- All 13 extras get new comments. Their 'Not in the row file / no row' text becomes false once the rows are applied, and 0x80d03e / 0x80d046 would otherwise lose round 95's code description.
- 0x80ccf6 filtered_engine_speed and 0x80ccf4 engine_speed are confirmed together (the old names had swapped meanings).

- 17 rows 0x8016b0-0x801718, 9 rows 0x803410-0x803424 and 0x80373c: no absolute, register-based or RAM-pointer access, zero in the dump, and no e2m record.
